I brought one of my large dogs to this veterinary clinic for an initial visit after I learned that the clinic is owned by my neighbor . At the time, I was considering switching to this clinic, but before making a final decision, I witnessed a disturbing incident involving the veterinarian’s American Bully and a UPS delivery driver.

While walking my dogs along the road, I encountered the UPS driver leaving the property after an apparent dog-bite incident. I stopped to speak with him near the end of the veterinarian’s driveway, approximately 400 feet from the house, and asked what had happened.

The driver told me that he had been bitten by the dog and believed an adult male on the property had prompted the dog to bite him. He did not identify the man, and I cannot independently verify his belief about what led to the incident. The driver also asked whether I had information about the property owner because, according to him, she was refusing to provide the information he needed to  file a dog bite claim.

What made this encounter particularly disturbing was something I recall the veterinarian telling me during my earlier visit, She expressed this as a joke:  that her American Bully had been trained not to let Black people near the property. Given the circumstances the UPS driver described, I found that statement deeply troubling. I cannot independently establish what led to the reported bite, but the combination of what I recalled being told and what the driver shared with me raised serious concerns.

I subsequently heard accounts from other neighbors describing additional alleged incidents involving animals on the property. These included reports of further aggressive behavior by the same American Bully. One neighbor also described a serious incident in which the veterinarian’s male horse allegedly injured her female horse. I did not personally witness these additional incidents, so I cannot independently verify the accounts. However, they contributed to my concerns about animal management and safety on the property.

I was initially reluctant to write this review. Since selling my property and moving away, I have felt more comfortable sharing my experience and explaining why I ultimately decided not to switch.

I understand that a veterinary review should reflect a person’s own experiences and observations. I have tried to distinguish what I personally witnessed from what the UPS driver told me and what other neighbors subsequently shared with me. I believe prospective clients deserve the opportunity to make informed decisions about whom they trust to care for their animals.

Based on my experience and the concerns it raised, I decided against switching to this clinic. I encourage prospective clients to ask questions about animal handling, safety practices, and the management of animals on the property before deciding whether this clinic is the right choice for them.

My visit here was quite terrible, we booked an appointment for our cat Bruce W. at 9:00am, we understand emergencies happen and were told our room was given away for an urgent case. Okay not a problem, the issue is they allow dogs to be off leash & misbehave, additionally the poor front desk girl is overworked, she was doing check in, check out, new patient paperwork, cleaning rooms, answering phone calls all by herself etc. We finally get called back into a room and the vet tech asked for records, I informed her we already gave everything to the front desk to scan in, but still handed over my original records, moving on, I am telling the technician that I feel that my cat may have TriTrich, he was just adopted from a rescue, has wet eyes with discharge and cow-pie like stool with a very bad smell  and we brought fecal to be tested, mind you I also mentioned to this the front desk when giving the reason for the appointment. They test his stool, do some bloodwork and then tell me the doctor will come in for an exam, the doctor on call comes in, no exam is done in front of us, she just says everything looks great, he might just have tummy issues due to food changes, I asked okay so he tested negative for TriTrich right? And she was like uhh no that has to be sent out, okay so why is it that I’ve been mentioning this over and over again and we weren’t informed of the option to send it out? So I tell her well I wish we were informed of that prior because we would have opted to have it sent out, she doesn’t have much to say, so then I ask about flea prevention and she is acting confused as I ask mentioned this to the tech, and states I am not the regular vet here so I think he might need Revolution Baby or Pink, but I can check, she gave us no real answers, and didn’t even seem like a knowledgeable licensed professional. My concerns were not taken seriously, and then they informed us at checkout we couldn’t use CareCredit unless it was $350 minimum which is outrageously high and I’ve never had that issue with a vet clinic before. Overall they are overpriced, understaffed, not smart and non-reassuring or do through exams. Save your money & time and look elsewhere. We DO NOT RECOMMEND.

Dr G's front desk scheduled an appointment for the same day. Both Rachel & Dr G were very thorough, patient, professional & compassionate.  They gave us time to think the options through & make a decision. They could have wanted their own films but used the current ones my vet sent over with the referral, which saved us money. Unfortunately, some places might take advantage of a very emotional time, to run unnecessary tests which is more cost to the bill. This was not the case & by taking small steps before going on to the next test, they kept the expense down & no unnecessary tests.
